hardware_trial.correction: An earlier version of this record said the trial found no authentication process identity at its immediate /proc PID/start-time check. The tl log shows that check passed; the exit was detected at the first liveness poll. Corrected after the offline analysis in auth-exit-offline-analysis.json.
hardware_trial.kind: one-shot OpenIPC kernel with stock userland; not the final OpenIPC rootfs
hardware_trial.log_source: flash TL mailbox, read after stock return
hardware_trial.probable_cause: Configuration rejected at parse time: the generated wpa.conf began with update_config=0, a global field that this CONFIG_NO_CONFIG_WRITE build of wpa_supplicant 2.11 does not parse. Under qemu-arm the same executable and configuration exit with status 255 within 0.03 s, and removing only that line keeps it running. Probable, not confirmed: the hardware exit status was not captured.
hardware_trial.startup_failure_observation: The start-time identity check passed: the trial logged the authentication start 9.37 s after boot and verified its start checkpoint in tl at 9.79 s. The process was already gone at the first liveness poll, within about 0.9 s of launch, before any fixed authentication event. The trial script of this revision did not record the exit status.
unconfirmed_causes: other immediate launch or exit failure

limitations: This is not a successful full OpenIPC migration. Authentication, DHCP and the stability window did not pass.
The current bakfs contains the authenticated trial image, not a vendor appfs recovery backup.
No raw logs, firmware, dumps, credentials, network identifiers, private hashes or run identifiers are included.
Any further physical trial or redelivery requires new explicit authorization; final migration remains blocked.

offline_trial_validation.extraction_note: The SquashFS inodes encoded 0755 for executable files. A first host extraction under umask 077 appeared as 0700; re-extraction with child umask 000 inside a private 0700 parent confirmed all exact inode modes without altering the image.
